counts_note: 220 completions per model: 80 arith + 30 code + 30 graph + 80 reference.

generator.code_oracle: AST interpreter, step budget 10000, no subprocess and no wall clock.

grader.code_rule: last fenced block; rstrip each line; drop one trailing empty line
grader.integer_rule: last line matching ^####[ \t]+(-?\d[\d,]*)[ \t]*$; no bare-number fallback
grader.invalid_policy: unparsable or truncated is invalid and counts as wrong in the primary accuracy

comparisons: accuracy, invalid rate, truncated rate, and accuracy among parsed, for arith_word, code_output, graph_path, and gsm8k indexes 0..79
per model, Newcombe 95% interval for arith_word accuracy minus gsm8k accuracy
trivial baseline: uniform draw from that family's observed oracle answers; for graph_path also the direct-edge weight when an edge exists
reporting.inclusion_rule: A committed item is in time iff the L1 block timestamp of its Turbo bundle is less than or equal to unlock_unix - 600, the bundle id is in that block, and the data-item bytes hash to the committed sha256 at the payload offset. The timestamp, height, and hash must agree on at least two independent gateways. ario.zigza.xyz is operated by the author and never counts as one of those two. HTTP 404, 429, and timeouts are UNKNOWN, not FAIL. The author's observation at release time is recorded and is not decisive. A batch is INVALID only when this check proves a timestamp after the deadline.
reporting.interval: Wilson 95% on each accuracy. Newcombe hybrid score 95% on arith_word minus gsm8k.
reporting.invalid_and_no_show: An unparsable answer is invalid. A completion with no end-of-text marker, or with a llama.cpp run count at least n_predict-1, is truncated and counts as invalid in the primary accuracy. Both are reported separately, and accuracy among parsed excludes them. A crashed item is retried once with the same flags and both logs are kept. A partial model is published as partial and is not dropped or trimmed. A batch is INVALID only under the inclusion rule. Unknown observation is not INVALID.
reporting.minimum_detectable_effect: At p=0.5, the Wilson 95% half-width is about 11 percentage points at n=80 and about 18 points at n=30. The Newcombe half-width of an arith-minus-gsm8k difference at n=80 is about 16 points. Items that share a template are not independent, so these are lower bounds on the uncertainty.
not_claimed: The GSM8K prefix is not difficulty-matched to arith_word.
A gap inside the minimum detectable effect is reported and is not called contamination.
No model-versus-model comparison is a headline result.
reporting.primary_endpoint: Per model and per family, accuracy with invalid and truncated answers counted as wrong.

runtime.binary_note: The executable is the launcher. shared_libraries are the hashed compute code.
runtime.n_predict_note: Phase 1 at n_predict 320 truncated 20/200 GSM8K completions (Qwen 5/50, Gemma 5/50, Ministral 2/50, Falcon 8/50) and the hit_cap flag was always false. EOS maxima were 292 to 318. 768 is above that observed maximum. The truncation rate at 768 was not measured, because those 20 completions were censored.
runtime.reasoning_note: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 is the non-thinking variant. reasoning off is a parser flag, not a capability switch.

seed_spec: enc(b) = uint32be(len(b)) || b. seed = SHA-256(enc(utf8('sealedbench/v2')) || enc(utf8(lowercase chain hash hex)) || enc(utf8(decimal round)) || enc(signature bytes) || enc(32-byte batch secret)). family_seed = SHA-256(enc(utf8('sealedbench/v2/family')) || enc(seed) || enc(utf8(family)) || enc(utf8(decimal n))). The JSON randomness field is not an input. It must still equal hex(SHA-256(signature)).

spec.author_limitation: The author chose the 32-byte batch secret and knows it. The author does not know the beacon signature, so the author cannot list the items before the round. Publishing this repository does not reveal the items.
spec.canonical_json: json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=True) plus a trailing newline per item.
spec.prng: SHA-256(key || uint64be(counter)), counter from 0, rejection sampling on the first 8 bytes.
spec.seed: enc(b) = uint32be(len(b)) || b. seed = SHA-256(enc(utf8('sealedbench/v2')) || enc(utf8(lowercase chain hash hex)) || enc(utf8(decimal round)) || enc(signature bytes) || enc(32-byte batch secret)). family_seed = SHA-256(enc(utf8('sealedbench/v2/family')) || enc(seed) || enc(utf8(family)) || enc(utf8(decimal n))). The JSON randomness field is not an input. It must still equal hex(SHA-256(signature)).
spec.test_secret_note: The published test secret is not the batch secret. Vectors do not predict this batch.

system_prompts.arith_word: Solve the grade-school math problem. Show brief reasoning, then end with a line exactly of the form #### <integer> and nothing after it.
system_prompts.code_output: Determine the exact standard output of the Python 3 program. After any reasoning, put that output and only that output in one fenced code block. The last fenced block is graded. Do not add commentary inside the fence.
system_prompts.graph_path: Solve the shortest-path problem on the undirected weighted graph. Show brief reasoning, then end with a line exactly of the form #### <integer> and nothing after it.
system_prompts.gsm8k_reference: Solve the grade-school math problem. Show brief reasoning, then end with a line exactly of the form #### <integer> and nothing after it.
